newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican opposition cry fraud in two state races.
newsitem.headline: Mexican opposition cry fraud in two state races.

text.p: Mexican opposition parties on Tuesday cried foul in two gubernatorial races held during Sunday's mid-term vote, saying the ruling party cheated them of victory and vowing to protest the result.

In the northern state of Sonora, the conservative National Action Party (PAN) rejected preliminary results showing their gubernatorial candidate Enrique Salgado Bojorquez a runner-up in the state race.
Salgado said in a statement the governing Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) used dirty tricks such as vote buying to pull out the race and said he could prove it.

With 97.7 percent of the vote counted, Salgado had polled 32.3 percent of ballots while his PRI opponent Armando Lopez Nogales had garnered 41.3 percent of the vote. Final results were due out on Wednesday.
Salgado alleged that in state's main districts there were more ballots cast than registered voters and that in all cases the ballots were for the gubernatorial race.

"It is impossible to accept, that in a state where the opposition governs 84 percent of the municipalities, the PRI claims it won the gubernatorial race," Salgado said. "Besides, the PRI lost its majority in the state congress and lost every race for federal congress, according to the results."
In the southern state of Campeche, it was the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) saying it was cheated of a state win.

Some 12,000 people led by PRD state candidate Layda Sansores took to the streets of the state capital to protest alleged fraud by the PRI, chanting "We're with you Layda," "We want no more fraud," and "Campechans unite."

"With proof we have in our hands, the electoral ballots themselves, we can demonstrate the irregularities. We will present our protest through legal means," said Juan Gonzalez Reyes, the PRD's representative to the state electoral body.
Tuesday's march started with only a few hundred people amid a torrential downpour, but citizens came out of their homes to join the protest in a state of just 200,000 residents.
Preliminary results with 91.4 percent of the vote counted showed PRI candidate Antonio Gonzalez Curi leading with 48.08 percent of the vote compared to 40.52 percent for Sansores.
